Signs they might be ready

Readiness isn't about age — it's a cluster of signs showing up together. Here's what I look for before we build a plan.

01

Physical control

Staying dry for two or more hours at a stretch, or waking from naps dry, and being able to get to the bathroom, undress, and sit still for a few minutes.

02

Body awareness

Noticing when they're going, or just after — an early sign their body and brain are starting to connect.

03

Communication

Able to tell you — in words, signs, or their own way — that they need to go, and generally follows simple two-step directions.

04

Interest

Curious about the bathroom, wants to wear "big kid" underwear, or has started asking about the potty on their own.

05

Independence

Actually wants to try things themselves — getting dressed, washing hands — even if it's slower or messier than doing it for them.

Before you start the clock

Signs you're ready too

Your mindset

You're aiming to coach, not rush — this tends to go better as a few unhurried weeks than a single weekend.

Your time

You've got a real stretch of days without travel, a big move, or a new sibling arriving, so accidents aren't competing with everything else.

Your response to accidents

You can treat them as information, not a setback — what they tell you matters more than how anyone reacts to them.

Your energy

You're genuinely up for being the cheerleader here, even on day four, when it's not going in a straight line.

Common questions

What if we start and it's clearly not working?

That's useful information, not failure. We pause, wait a few weeks, and try again once more of the signs are actually there.

Is there a "right" age?

No single number — most children show enough of the signs somewhere between about 2 and 3.5 years, but it's genuinely different child to child.

Do you give us a day-by-day plan?

Yes — once I understand your child and your household's routine, you get a plan built around your days, not a generic script.

Let's build your plan

A few quick questions so I understand where you're starting from — takes about two minutes.
